grep --perl-regexp: deliberate: this is the PCRE engine, including syntax and matching semantics not provided by the bytewise basic/extended/fixed engines. A partial recognizer would silently answer the wrong language.
grep -P: deliberate: short alias for the unimplemented PCRE engine; it is rejected rather than approximated with extended regular expressions.
sed --debug: deliberate: GNU's execution trace and annotated-program diagnostic format, not command-result semantics. The interpreter rejects it rather than pretending to emit that debugging protocol.
sort --debug: deliberate: GNU's key annotation and diagnostic format, not ordering semantics. It is rejected rather than producing an incomplete diagnostic stream.
sort --general-numeric-sort: deliberate: exact GNU behavior is strtold ordering, including signed NaNs, infinities, hexadecimal floats, exponents, long-double range and architecture-specific rounding. It needs a shared cross-ISA general-number parser/comparator; a decimal-only approximation would silently misorder data.
sort --random-source: deliberate: this supplies entropy to GNU random-sort, which is itself outside this deterministic sort's surface. Accepting and ignoring the source would falsely claim reproducible randomized ordering.
sort -g: deliberate: short alias for GNU's strtold-based general numeric ordering. It is rejected until the full cross-ISA number syntax and comparison contract exists.
uname --all: deliberate: the operating system name is not in struct utsname and is not ours to claim on another system's behalf. This one answers Moonwater, and -a stops at the machine for the same reason.
uname --operating-system: deliberate: the operating system name is not in struct utsname and is not ours to claim on another system's behalf. This one answers Moonwater, and -a stops at the machine for the same reason.
uname -a: deliberate: the operating system name is not in struct utsname and is not ours to claim on another system's behalf. This one answers Moonwater, and -a stops at the machine for the same reason.
uname -o: deliberate: the operating system name is not in struct utsname and is not ours to claim on another system's behalf. This one answers Moonwater, and -a stops at the machine for the same reason.
diff -c: deliberate: context format is a separate output protocol, not an alias for unified output; it is rejected until its headers, ranges, separators and no-newline markers are complete.
diff -C: deliberate: valued short spelling of the unimplemented context output protocol; approximating it with unified output would silently emit the wrong patch language.
diff --context: deliberate: optional-count long spelling of context output, rejected with the rest of that output protocol.
diff -e: deliberate: ed-script output is executable command language with escaping and final-line rules of its own; normal diff output is not a safe approximation.
diff --ed: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented ed-script output protocol.
diff -n: deliberate: RCS-script output is a separate executable patch language and is rejected rather than approximated.
diff --rcs: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented RCS output protocol.
diff -y: deliberate: side-by-side layout needs display-width, tab and truncation semantics; emitting normal diff output would falsely claim that layout.
diff --side-by-side: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented side-by-side renderer.
diff -W: deliberate: width controls only the unimplemented side-by-side renderer and is rejected rather than accepted without effect.
diff --width: deliberate: long spelling of the side-by-side width control; accepting it while ignoring the width would be a silent lie.
diff --left-column: deliberate: modifier for the unimplemented side-by-side output protocol.
diff --suppress-common-lines: deliberate: modifier for the unimplemented side-by-side output protocol.
diff -p: deliberate: C-function hunk annotations require a source recognizer and alter the patch headers; they are rejected rather than omitted silently.
diff --show-c-function: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented C-function hunk annotation.
diff -F: deliberate: regex-selected function-line annotations alter every hunk header and need the regex engine plus exact header quoting.
diff --show-function-line: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented regex function-line annotation.
diff -t: deliberate: output tab expansion changes patch bytes and needs column tracking across every output format; comparison-time -E is implemented, this renderer is not.
diff --expand-tabs: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented output tab renderer.
diff --initial-tab: deliberate: output alignment modifier with format-specific tab placement, rejected rather than ignored.
diff --tabsize: deliberate: tab-stop control affects output rendering and -E comparison semantics; only the standard eight-column comparison contract is implemented.
diff --suppress-blank-empty: deliberate: format-specific output whitespace suppression, rejected rather than changing comparison data.
diff -l: deliberate: pagination delegates to pr and changes process/error behavior; this freestanding tool does not claim that external rendering pipeline.
diff --paginate: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented pr pagination pipeline.
diff --no-dereference: deliberate: exact symlink-object comparison requires lstat/readlink traversal throughout recursive diff; following links is the current explicit policy.
diff --ignore-file-name-case: deliberate: case-insensitive directory pairing needs collision rules for two names which fold alike; bytewise pairing remains explicit.
diff -x: deliberate: recursive name exclusion needs repeatable ordered glob storage and directory-level matching; it is rejected rather than applying a partial basename filter.
diff --exclude: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented recursive exclusion matcher.
diff -X: deliberate: exclude-file parsing adds newline, escaping, empty-pattern and read-error contracts; no partial reader is advertised.
diff --exclude-from: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented exclusion-file grammar.
diff -S: deliberate: starting-file changes top-level directory merge ordering and needs exact interaction with exclusions and case-folding.
diff --starting-file: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented directory starting point.
diff --from-file: deliberate: one-to-many comparison changes operand arity, headings and worst-status aggregation; it is not a two-file alias.
diff --to-file: deliberate: reverse one-to-many comparison changes operand arity, headings and status aggregation.
diff -I: deliberate: ignore-matching-lines needs regex matching per complete change group; ignoring individual matching lines would produce a plausible but wrong script.
diff --ignore-matching-lines: deliberate: long spelling of group-aware regex change suppression.
diff -D: deliberate: ifdef merge output is source generation with directive placement and incomplete-line rules, not a normal diff variant.
diff --ifdef: deliberate: long spelling of the unimplemented ifdef merge generator.
diff --line-format: deliberate: GNU's line/group format language is a printf-like interpreter; accepting a subset would silently generate corrupt output.
diff -d: deliberate: minimal mode changes the edit-search guarantee on large repeated inputs; the GNU-compatible heuristic matcher cannot claim it as a no-op.
diff --minimal: deliberate: long spelling of the stronger unimplemented minimal-edit guarantee.
diff --horizon-lines: deliberate: this changes the matcher search horizon and therefore edit selection; it is rejected rather than accepted without effect.
diff --color: deliberate: ANSI coloring changes the output byte protocol and requires WHEN policy plus palette handling; plain deterministic patches remain the contract.
diff --palette: deliberate: palette is meaningful only with the unimplemented color output protocol and cannot safely be ignored.
